title: Kamarajar and the River Dam Irrigation Revolution: Transforming Agriculture in Tamil Nadu
summary: Between 1954 and 1963, Chief Minister K. Kamaraj launched an unprecedented irrigation revolution, constructing major reservoir projects to eradicate rural drought.
keywords: Historical Dialogue 178: நேருவும் “ஜெனரல்கள் தீர்ந்துவிட்டால்?” என்ற கேள்வியும்
full_text:
When K. Kamaraj assumed office as Chief Minister in 1954, vast agricultural tracts across Tamil Nadu were crippled by recurring droughts and monsoonal failures.

Summoning chief irrigation engineers to his secretariat, Kamaraj spread out topographical survey maps across the table:
"Look at these seasonal rivers. During the monsoon, millions of gallons of freshwater surge through our riverbeds and empty wastefully into the sea. Yet during summer, our farmers gaze desperately at cloudless skies for a single drop of water. This madness must stop!"

Engineers cautioned that executing multiple simultaneous dam projects would strain state finances and require immense steel and cement quotas:
"Chief Minister, such ambitious river valley projects require immense capital."

Kamaraj responded with decisive authority:
"If we lack funds, I will travel to New Delhi and secure them from Pandit Nehru! Spare no effort and cut through bureaucratic red tape. Construct reservoirs across every viable catchment area. When water flows into the farmer’s furrow, the entire state prospers!"

Over the next nine years, Kamaraj completed an astonishing array of major irrigation projects: the Bhavanisagar Dam, Vaigai Dam, Manimuthar Dam, Amaravathi Dam, Sathanur Dam, Krishnagiri Dam, and the inter-state Parambikulam-Aliyar Project.

Kamaraj’s vision brought millions of acres under assured cultivation, transforming rural Tamil Nadu into an agricultural powerhouse.
